answers.answer: Each player takes 12 ordinary turns: 4 seasons × 3 ordinary rounds. Courtship is an event with no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.

Hosting order: rotate servants (Quarters→Available, then Expended→Quarters, one space each); resolve round event, then ongoing tile effects; choose an activity tile; invite exactly the printed number/types of gentry; provide every required service; take favours, resolving all positives before negatives; optionally buy one tile; cleanup by sending used servants to Expended, played gentry to personal discard, and returning/flipping the activity tile as required. After cleanup only the last player in order advances the marker. Events occur after rotation and before ongoing effects.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure—Hosting an activity; Round-track events

answers.answer: Passing order: all servants directly to Available Service; recover all gentry in your discard to hand; resolve the round event, then ongoing tile effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. Servants used for ongoing effects are expended at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.

Yes. Four Service Help actions cost 12 reputation increments, taking 6.1 to 3.4, and are legal while above the 1.1 minimum. Each can move one servant only from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, never from Expended Service. Screening uses the reputation fixed at the end of step 2 (6.1), so the PR6 tile and guests remain legal even after actual reputation falls to 3.4.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions; Special Rules & Edge Cases

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours, choosing order within each group. At minimum, you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid losing reputation; losses stop at 1.1. A money penalty must be fully payable: use positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money as needed; if you cannot fund it, you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity—Enjoy favours; Reputation, wealth and special actions

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments, gain £100, repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments, move one servant from Quarters to Available, repeatable. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments, fully refresh Market, once per turn. At 1.1 you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.

Host Butler’s Room with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants, excluding underbutlers, from Servants for Hire into Expended Service; there is no fee. Used butler is expended and the tile upgrades on first use. Its upgraded side instead permits recruiting one common servant (footman, valet, or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; unique servants cannot be recruited.

A housekeeper substitutes for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even when that regular type is available.

The only way to acquire an underbutler is to buy Butler’s Pantry; it goes immediately to Expended Service. It is not immediately available: normally it moves to Quarters at the next service rotation and Available at the second subsequent rotation. Passing or Refresh Service can make it available sooner; once in Quarters, Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can enable earlier use. Opponents cannot recruit it.

Pay the Market space price plus the tile’s printed modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot be below £100. You can never acquire a duplicate tile you already own. Reputation does not restrict purchase, so a tile above your reputation may be bought.

When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on its matching Market tile and another is drawn; duplicate stack shares one space/price. Reserve-eligible tiles go straight to Reserve and are replaced by another draw. When filling multiple spaces, sort only the newly drawn tiles by sorting number. Buying one from a two-tile stack leaves the space occupied, so there is no refill.

After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws also go directly there, with the same exception. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve and later PR1 draws go there too. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. After each of the first three courtships a full Market refresh is standard, after Reserve movement; this remains true even if no tiles moved.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve; Courtship and seasonal upkeep; Overview

answers.answer: At courtship, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. For courtships 1–3, score tile VP for the current face-up theme (including negatives; only the face-up hybrid category counts). Highest score takes one VP card and chooses one Fairchild. On a tie, each tied player draws a VP card and no one gets a Fairchild. Everyone discards one objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and put them at the bottom of the deck. Seasonal upkeep then opens Reserve, refreshes Market, reveals the next theme to the right of prior themes, passes first-player marker anticlockwise, and advances the round marker.

Final courtship scores tile VP across all four revealed themes, counting repeated categories repeatedly; the highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild. A tie is broken by reputation level (wheel position ignored); if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the tie rule. Discard the final objective. Then players get a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible, move marker to Wedding Bells, and score.

End-game categories: face-up printed VP on all improvement tiles (including negatives), gentry in hand and discard (including negatives/family/final Fairchild), fulfilled objectives, reputation, servants, wealth, and retained VP cards. Reputation levels 1–7 score 1/3/6/10/15/21/28 VP; wheel position has no effect. Wealth is 1 VP per £200, rounded down. Victory ties: final Fairchild wins; otherwise higher reputation level wins; if still tied, share victory.

Normally start with 5 objectives and draw 2 at round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving 3 to score. Shuffle simultaneous discards together before placing face down at bottom of objective deck. Extra objectives from Main Library or a VP card add to final retained count and do not cause an extra discard. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles at game end, not upgrading them.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards; Courtship and seasonal upkeep

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, on any later own turn (multiple cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring, for its benefit instead of printed VP. Used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused VP cards stay hidden with objectives and score printed VP at game end.

A normal activity tile must flip to its upgrade side after first use; subsequent use while already upgraded leaves it upgraded. Hybrids start with the underlined category up and flip after every use, moving to the newly face-up category. A tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument hosts only once, upgrades into the monument, and cannot host again; its monument benefit begins on later turns. For hybrids only the face-up category counts for courtship and objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects—Normal activity tiles, Hybrids, Monuments

answers.answer: Monuments give one reputation during the ongoing-effects step on ordinary hosting and passing turns, but no income on courtship; a newly bought monument starts paying on a later turn. Servants’ Hall works during that same ongoing-effects step on hosting or passing: place one available servant on it, reduce one opponent by one reputation and gain one yourself; that servant goes to Expended at turn end. It cannot target a player at minimum reputation.

Heritage Guest Suite: one casual guest from hand, footman on tile plus guest’s normal service; double all guest favours, including negatives; remains an activity tile after upgrade. Queen’s Suite: one prestige guest from hand, housekeeper on tile plus guest’s normal service; double one chosen favour and resolve others normally; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: draw one prestige guest from deck to attend, butler on tile and no guest personal service; double nonnegative favours, excluding negatives; guest is kept and discarded at cleanup; upgrades into a monument. Each has fixed count one, which cannot be increased or decreased.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table; suite count rule

answers.answer: Choose a random first player. Starting with that player’s left and going clockwise, players choose an available base family board. Bonuses: Asquith gets the Dowager Countess (fifth family card); Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gets £300; York gets a footman in Available Service.

Each player starts reputation level 1, position 1, with the 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters stacked with 1 showing and Max at bottom; no 7/8 counters. Starting servants in Available Service: butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid, footman. Starting tiles: Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green, starter/building icon showing. Family cards: Lord, Lady, Heir, Young Lady. Among family bonuses, only Ponsonby starts with money (£300).
For three players: 3 valets, 3 lady’s maids, 6 footmen, and 2 underbutlers. No butlers or housekeepers are stocked. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable for the game.

Separate and shuffle starter guests from the casual deck; deal two to each player’s hand. Shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon, not a separate guest type.
answers.evidence: Setup; Gentry, screening, dismissal and family

answers.answer: For four players, select one double-sided monument per player plus one: 5 monuments. You may select at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count against the setup selection.

Draw until six different eligible Market spaces are filled: tiles with PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside and return them to the bag after filling. Stack eligible duplicates in their matching space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort spaces by ascending sorting number beginning at £300. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments are ineligible.

Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme face up and keep revealed themes in order throughout the game. Put base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall. The first theme is not hidden and old themes remain revealed when new ones are added.

At hosting rotation, the servant in Quarters moves to Available Service; the servant in Expended moves to Quarters. Each moves one space and neither is moved twice. An available servant you do not use remains available.

The Village Fair event resolves before activity selection, so an unupgraded Private Study does not earn the reward on that turn even if hosted/upgraded later. An already-upgraded Study immediately gives £300 and 2 reputation on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9 only.

Space 6 Draw Objectives resolves before ongoing tile effects, after rotation on a host turn or after servants and discarded gentry return on a pass. Draw two and keep both secret with your other objectives. Passing players receive the event too.
Yes. National Holiday waives PR requirements for all tiles and guests while hosting, even if reputation is lower. All other requirements still apply, including service and exact gentry counts/types.

Yes. Builders’ Holiday allows any number from Market and/or Reserve within funds. Finish all purchases before sliding/refilling; each uses the original space or Reserve price plus printed modifier from the unchanged market. No refresh between purchases by special action or VP card. Market Purchase VP card uses the same multi-buy/unchanged-market rule.
answers.evidence: Round-track events; Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside and leave Reserve unchanged. Refill all six Market spaces under normal refill rules; after filling, return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix. Thus removed tiles cannot appear in that same refresh; Reserve tiles remain in Reserve.

Each reputation symbol changes one increment. Move clockwise to gain and anticlockwise to lose; crossing 5→1 raises a level and 1→5 lowers one. Minimum is 1.1 and standard maximum is 7.5 (Max.5); ignore losses beyond minimum. At Max.5, excess is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; you can take special actions before or in the middle of resolving a reputation favour to make room.
Money is public. Players cannot give or receive money between them. Costs cannot exceed holdings; penalties must be fully payable. The common supply is unlimited; use proxies if it runs out.

For “two ladies,” any female family member or female guest can count; for “two casual guests,” only casual guests count, not family. Invite exactly the printed count/types—no extra or fewer. Family requires no personal service and has no PR; guests are subject to normal PR screening unless National Holiday.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity—Invite gentry; Reputation screening

answers.answer: Ordinary invites are played from hand and revealed as attendees. For a screening invite, draw the stated number, choose the stated number to keep, reveal only the kept cards, and add kept cards to hand. Put rejected cards on the bottom of the corresponding guest deck without revealing them.

Dismissal is optional; if you have no unwanted guest you need not dismiss. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, the current activity, or discard, including one drawn earlier in the same Enjoy Favours step. Family cannot be dismissed. A dismissed guest goes to bottom of matching guest deck, is no longer yours, is not recovered on passing, and does not score later.

Lord: £200. Lady: choose screening two casual guests/keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. The Lady and Heir offer choices; Lord has one benefit; Dowager gives both.

The Young Lady’s bonus requires a male prestige guest. A male casual guest does not qualify; a female prestige guest does not qualify; Charles Fairchild is male and a prestige guest, so qualifies. The bonus is two reputation. She still draws one casual guest in every case.

Charles is a male prestige guest, has no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest, has no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. They are prestige guests, not family, so family dismissal immunity does not apply to them.

Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes you lose one yourself. Minimum-reputation protection applies: a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
A Barn gives one reputation every time you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile and passing do not trigger it.

The Servants’ Quarters tile lets you use one servant from Quarters per turn in addition to Available Service, without paying reputation; ordinary rotation instead moves servants one area (Quarters→Available, Expended→Quarters). Service Help costs 3 reputation increments and moves one servant from Quarters to Available. A servant used through the tile goes to Expended Service at turn end.

Private Study front: one butler and two family; no tile favour, then it upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile. Once upgraded, it cannot be hosted as an activity again. On Village Fair rounds 3 and 9 it gives £300 and 2 reputation without staffing or hosting.

Unupgraded Main Library: butler and two family, draw one extra objective. Upgraded: butler and three family, draw one VP card. The extra objective increases the number retained for final scoring and does not trigger an extra courtship discard.
answers.evidence: Main Library; Objectives and VP cards

answers.answer: Objective VP benefit: draw two objectives, keep one, put the other on the bottom of the objective deck. This adds one additional retained objective for final scoring and does not cause an extra discard.

Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available, including Expended, and they can be used immediately. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves only one from Quarters to Available, never directly from Expended.
Hire Servant VP card takes one servant from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutler, into Expended Service. It cannot be used for service immediately from there.

Yes. Refresh Guest returns one gentry of choice, including a family member, from personal discard to hand. If used before Invite Gentry, you may select that returned card to attend the activity, subject to normal requirements; return alone does not automatically play it.

The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper and underbutler. Ordinary servant scoring is 2 VP per servant of every type/location; the ten-servant objective awards 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
Yes. Upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite count as monuments (3 VP per monument). For category objectives, a hybrid counts in its currently face-up category only.

Nature Group is 11 VP: own Flower Room and one garden (English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze). Domestic Group is 12 VP: own Gabled Conservatory and either Main Library or North Library. Owning at game end suffices; tiles need not have been used or upgraded.

The prestige-guest objective counts each prestige guest, excluding family; a final Fairchild is a prestige guest and counts. The every-three-guests objective counts groups of three nonfamily guests; incomplete groups score nothing.

The reputation objective gives 7 VP for maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective gives 10 VP for at least £1200. Wheel position has no effect on ordinary reputation VP or reputation tie resolution; only level matters.

Both West Terrace sides require one butler and exactly three family. Unupgraded favour: draw one prestige guest. Upgraded favour: draw one prestige guest and optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity or discard to the bottom of their matching decks. It remains an activity tile, not an ongoing dismissal tile.
There is no hand or discard-pile limit. Gentry in discard remain yours and score normally; passing returns them to hand.
You may inspect all Reserve tiles and buy any one, including a tile under another in a stack; there is no top-only restriction. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.

You are not required to host whenever possible; you may pass. If your preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.

Yes. On a pass you can use the free Market refresh benefit, one paid special-action refresh (4 reputation increments), and multiple Market Refresh VP cards in the same turn. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the special-action Refresh Market; free passing refreshes and VP-card refreshes are separate. (The summary also says no refresh between purchases within a Builders’ Holiday or Market Purchase multi-buy sequence.)
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions; Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card
